stances.claim: Despite reader speculation, there is no evidence linking PFM, IRM, or Danding Cojuangco to Ninoy's murder -- CJ's answer in 2009 was No, and his answer now remains No.

The Agrava Board -- created Oct 22, 1983 after the first Fernando committee was criticized for bias, with Corazon Agrava as chair, Andres Narvasa as general counsel, and Bienvenido Tan Jr. as public coordinator -- conducted 125 sessions, heard 194 witnesses, and produced 20,377 pages of transcript, concluding that several military officers including Fabian Ver conspired to kill Ninoy.

The Pamaran SBN decision (Dec 2, 1985) acquitting all accused was nullified post-EDSA by the reconstituted Supreme Court as a 'sham,' and the SBN re-trial led to J Hermosisima's 177-page Sept 28, 1990 conviction of 16 soldiers including Brig. Gen. Luther Custodio -- Ver, however, was never convicted because the SBN never acquired jurisdiction over him (he fled with PFM to Hawaii on Feb 25, 1986 and died in Bangkok on Nov 21, 1998).

Bienvenido Tan Jr.'s March 15, 2009 letter to CJ -- and his book 'The Public Has the Right to Know' -- explicitly state that there was 'never any evidence linking President Marcos or Imelda or Danding' to the plot, and the two Aquino presidents (Cory and P-Noy) never objected to these court rulings, the book, or CJ's Inquirer columns.

Persida Acosta's August 2004 motion for a third trial -- premised on a claimed upward-trajectory bullet allegedly fired by Rolando Galman rather than CIC Rogelio Moreno -- was unanimously denied by J Puno's March 8, 2005 resolution, which held that the wound of entrance was higher than the wound of exit and rejected the deflection theory ('akin to a cartilage').

The Supreme Court has spoken unanimously, and 'to me, that should definitively settle the matter' -- even though none of the convicted soldiers, now pardoned and freed, has ever admitted responsibility.

notable_anecdotes: The Bienvenido Tan Jr. March 15, 2009 personal letter to CJ -- 'there was never any evidence linking President Marcos or Imelda or Danding so that much as we might have wanted to make a finding that they or any one of them was in the plot, we could not in good conscience come up with that conclusion' -- quoted in full as the most candid insider testimony.

The Agrava Board statistics -- 125 sessions, 194 witnesses, 20,377 pages of transcript -- recurring numerical motif (also deployed in A135) used as the credentialing signature of the most rigorous Philippine fact-finding effort ever convened.
The 'Gray Dean' epithet for Andres Narvasa -- UST faculty period nickname that later became CJ -- a rare CJ-style biographical detail showing professional intimacy with the figures named.

Ver's geographical fate -- fled to Hawaii Feb 25, 1986 with PFM; died in Bangkok Nov 21, 1998 'he never returned to our country' -- used to explain the procedural gap (no jurisdiction) without exonerating the man.

J Puno's scientific-forensic close -- 'It is unthinkable that the bullet, while projected upwards, would, instead of exiting to the roof of the head, go down to the mandible because it was allegedly deflected by a petrous bone which though hard is, in fact, a mere spongy protuberance, akin to a cartilage' -- one of the most vividly anatomical SC quotations in CJ's corpus.

The acknowledged loose end at close -- 'none of the convicted soldiers -- though already pardoned and freed -- has admitted any responsibility for the crime' -- honest narrative incompleteness despite asserting that the matter is settled.

one_paragraph_summary: After the Aug 21 commemoration of Ninoy Aquino's martyrdom at the Manila International Airport, readers again asked Panganiban whether President Ferdinand Marcos (PFM), First Lady Imelda Romualdez Marcos (IRM), or Eduardo 'Danding' Cojuangco were complicit in Ninoy's killing. CJ's answer in 2009 was No, and his answer now is still No. He recounts the fact-finding history: three days after the assassination, PFM created a CJ Enrique Fernando committee, soon criticized for bias; replaced on Oct 22, 1983 by the Agrava Board with Corazon Agrava as chair (later joined by Andres Narvasa as general counsel and Bienvenido Tan Jr. as public coordinator), which held 125 sessions, heard 194 witnesses, and consumed 20,377 pages of transcript, concluding that several military officers including Fabian Ver conspired to kill Ninoy. The Pamaran SBN decision (Dec 2, 1985) acquitting all accused was nullified post-EDSA by the reconstituted Supreme Court as a 'sham,' and J Regino Hermosisima Jr.'s 177-page re-trial decision (Sept 28, 1990) convicted 16 soldiers including Brig. Gen. Luther Custodio of double murder. Ver was never convicted because the SBN never acquired jurisdiction -- he fled with PFM to Hawaii on Feb 25, 1986 and died in Bangkok on Nov 21, 1998, never returning home. The SC denied the soldiers' petition for review on July 25, 1991. CJ then asked Tan Jr. directly why the Agrava Board did not name a mastermind; Tan's March 15, 2009 letter -- echoed in his book 'The Public Has the Right to Know' -- replied that 'there was never any evidence linking President Marcos or Imelda or Danding,' and the two Aquino presidents (Cory and P-Noy) never objected to the rulings, the book, or CJ's columns. The remaining controversy is who pulled the trigger: PAO chief Persida Acosta's Aug 2004 motion for a third trial argued for an upward-trajectory bullet allegedly fired by Rolando Galman, not CIC Rogelio Moreno. J Reynato S. Puno's unanimous March 8, 2005 resolution rejected the motion -- the wound of entrance was higher than the wound of exit, and the spongy-bone-deflection theory was 'unthinkable.' 'The Court had spoken unanimously,' and to CJ, that settles the matter -- even though none of the pardoned, freed soldiers has ever admitted responsibility.
